Rationale: HydroSHEDS: already hydrologically conditioned; consistent with HydroRIVERS (G05) and HydroBASINS (G06); recommended for hydrological analysis. Copernicus GLO-30: higher resolution (30m); better for local slope/erosion analysis; requires hydrologic conditioning. Recommend HydroSHEDS for primary analysis with Copernicus GLO-30 as supplementary check where resolution matters.
Applies_To: G09, G10, G11, G12, G13, G14 — all terrain derivatives inherit this decision
Notes: MUST be decided and documented before G09 processing begins. Once decided this cannot be changed without rebuilding all terrain derivatives and revalidating G24 flood hazard model.

Rationale: Degrees is the standard unit for geomorphological analysis and is used in most erosion severity classification systems including the LKP_ErosionSeverity.csv slope classes defined in Phase 1. Percent slope is more intuitive for engineering applications but less standard in hazard mapping. DECISION: Use DEGREES project-wide.
Applies_To: G10 Slope, DB03 Slope field, G24 flood hazard model, G27 erosion hotspot analysis, G31 hazard index
Notes: FIXED — do not change after G10 is computed. All downstream analyses referencing slope must use degrees. Slope classes in LKP_ErosionSeverity description fields should be updated to match degree thresholds at implementation.

Options_Considered: D8 (single direction) vs D-infinity (multi-direction) vs MFD (multiple flow direction)
Rationale: D8: standard; simple; widely supported; consistent with HydroSHEDS methodology; recommended for drainage network delineation. D-infinity: better for diffuse flow; more realistic on gentle slopes. MFD: most realistic but computationally intensive. Recommend D8 for consistency with HydroSHEDS source data.
Applies_To: G13 Flow Direction, G14 Flow Accumulation, G24 flood hazard
Notes: MUST be decided before G13 processing. D8 is recommended for consistency with HydroSHEDS.

Options_Considered: Sink-fill only vs Breach-depression vs Sink-fill + stream burn from G05
Rationale: Only relevant if Copernicus GLO-30 selected in DEC01. Stream burning (carving DEM along G05 river network) produces drainage network most consistent with observed rivers. Recommended: sink-fill + stream burn from G05.
Notes: Only required if DEC01 = Copernicus GLO-30

Options_Considered: ESA WorldCover v200 (2021 10m) vs alternative approved product
Rationale: ESA WorldCover 2021 at 10m is the highest quality globally consistent free land cover product currently available. The specification names it as the approved source. Confirm version and download before processing.
Notes: WorldCover 2021 version v200 is recommended. Document version at acquisition. If a newer version is released before baseline is published consider updating and documenting the change.

Rationale: Standard northwest illumination is conventional for cartographic hillshade in the northern hemisphere. Produces visually intuitive terrain representation for Nigeria study area. Use as default for all map outputs. Document if different settings used for specific maps.
Notes: Hillshade is for visualisation only — does not affect analytical outputs
